# SyntaxDiff

> Privacy-first, client-side syntax-aware diff. Diff structure, not bytes.

## About
SyntaxDiff is a browser-based tool that compares two code/config snippets (JSON, YAML, SQL, TOML, XML) and produces a Git-style diff of their *structure* — ignoring formatting and key order. It auto-detects the language, formats and recursively sorts keys, then diffs entirely in the browser via a Web Worker. No data leaves the machine.

## Core concepts
- Paste Source A and Source B, choose a language (or auto-detect), pick options, and Compare.
- The result is a read-only `/diff/:id` page in split (side-by-side) or unified view.
- Diffs are structural: object keys may be sorted; array order is always preserved.
- Local history is stored in IndexedDB in the browser only — there is no backend.

## How AI agents can use SyntaxDiff
- Canonicalize a config (sort keys) and compare structure across environments.
- Detect real schema/logic changes between two versions of a config while ignoring cosmetic key order or formatting.
